reason: The cited evidence shows a yield strength plateau in a related alloy (E1) and that SRO can be computationally induced in HfNbTaZr (E2), but none of the passages provide direct experimental evidence that SRO in HfNbTaTiZr raises dislocation barriers, reduces anharmonicity, or causes the predicted plateau and thermal expansion changes. The key mechanistic premises are thus unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: SRO can be induced in HfNbTaTiZr by annealing at ~1000°C and quenching
Enhanced SRO raises local energy barriers for dislocation motion
Enhanced SRO reduces lattice anharmonicity and thermal expansion
SRO-induced barriers cause a yield strength plateau at 673–1073 K
SRO effects are stable and dominant over this temperature range
